title: introduce-policy-translator-and-kms-audit-enhancer-with-residency-migration-tool
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We need a runtime shim that converts legacy role bindings into attribute-aware RBAC v2 decisions and attaches authoritative KMS/region metadata to audit events so downstream compliance tools can make deterministic residency decisions. This PR adds: 1) a policy-translator module that runs as a lightweight decision-time transformer to map old role bindings (operator/service-account) to attribute-based requests (zone, data_class, operator_scope); 2) an audit-enhancer that decorates audit entries with KMS key provenance, key-region, and residency-proof tokens generated from the KMS attestor; 3) a migration CLI (residencyctl migrate-rbac) to help operators backfill translated policies into the policy store for customers who opt-in; 4) end-to-end unit and integration tests and CI job updates. Scope: This is intended as a non-breaking rollout: the translator runs in shadow by default and can be flipped with a config flag. The audit-enhancer is enabled for Dedicated and Private installs only until we've completed perf validation for Hosted. Checklist: - [x] policy-translator implementation and unit tests - [x] audit-enhancer implementation and integration tests - [x] residencyctl migration CLI and docs - [x] feature flags + config gating (default: translator=shadow, enhancer=off for hosted) - [x] security review and threat model notes included - [x] changelog & release note entry Summary of commits: single logical feature branch, squashed into one merge commit. See commits list for brief commits. Backwards compatibility: translator runs in shadow mode; no role semantics change until operator opts to write translated policies via CLI. Risk: audit payloads now include additional KMS provenance fields — these are additive and sanitized for PII. Deployment notes: For Private, enable audit-enhancer after KMS attestor endpoint configuration. For Dedicated, start in shadow, monitor traffic, then opt-in. Related work: builds on ENG-3126 (rbacv2 decision API) and ENG-3950 (kms-attestor service).
